reviewed_by: Claude Code, root cause independently validated and the patch reviewed by a fresh subagent (code-troubleshooting skill)
reason: Live deploys saw GET /api/v1/deployment/status time out and then return HTTP 500 during project handoffs. Root cause: the supervisor serves status through coordinator.status(), which ran in a coordination write transaction and locked the single deployment_host row (_host); transfer() holds that row while waiting on project ownership, so status reads queued, each holding one of the supervisor's 4 pool connections, until the 30 s pool wait raised DatabaseBusyError, which the supervisor had no handler for. Fix: status() reads one unlocked snapshot (REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY on PostgreSQL) via _read_host, and the supervisor maps DatabaseBusyError to 503 with Retry-After like the execution kernel. Selected: test_deployment_status_snapshot.py (new: status answers while another transaction holds the host row; with no host row it reports the write defaults and creates nothing), test_runtime_management.py (new: the supervisor's 503 handler; existing deployment routes), test_deployment_lifecycle.py and test_runtime_project_roller.py (status consumers: handoffs, version targeting, roller).
exclusions: No UI, setting or chat journey changed; no frontend, Playwright or LAN-instance journey applies. The new regression tests reproduce the live lock with a real held row on PostgreSQL (staging container, throwaway schema) and fail without the fix. Remaining causes are follow-ups: transfer() still holds the host row while waiting on ownership, and the live pool budget pins 4 connections per process.
